claims.claim: Current major versions of the GitHub Actions used: actions/checkout v7, actions/setup-node v6, actions/cache v5, actions/github-script v9, aws-actions/configure-aws-credentials v6, pnpm/action-setup v6.
claims.raw_snippet: actions/checkout v7.0.0 is the latest release.

claims.claim: The default GITHUB_TOKEN has been read-only since February 2023, so write jobs need an explicit permissions block; OIDC role assumption requires permissions: id-token: write. Cron schedules run in UTC. ubuntu-latest currently resolves to Ubuntu 24.04. Use $GITHUB_OUTPUT / $GITHUB_ENV (set-output/save-state are deprecated).
claims.raw_snippet: The default permissions for the GITHUB_TOKEN can be set to read-only; to use OIDC you must set permissions with id-token: write. Scheduled workflows use POSIX cron syntax and run on UTC time.

claims.claim: The Hebcal REST API provides Jewish-calendar and Shabbat-times JSON (holidays, candle-lighting) used to drive Shabbat/holiday-aware deploy freezes.
claims.raw_snippet: Hebcal provides JSON APIs for Jewish holidays (/hebcal) and Shabbat times (/shabbat) with cfg=json.

claims.claim: The Hebcal holidays JSON endpoint for a given year/month and geonameid (281184 = Jerusalem) returns major holidays.
claims.raw_snippet: The /hebcal endpoint with cfg=json, maj=on, year, month, geo=geoname and geonameid returns Jewish holiday events as JSON.

claims.claim: Templated Hebcal holidays endpoint examples use placeholders for year/month/geonameid that the workflow substitutes at runtime.
claims.raw_snippet: The /hebcal endpoint accepts year, month and geonameid parameters; examples show {YEAR}/{MONTH}/{ID} placeholders.

claims.claim: Shell-variable form of the Hebcal holidays endpoint used inside bash steps.
claims.raw_snippet: The /hebcal endpoint is called from bash with $YEAR, $MONTH and $GEONAMEID shell variables; yto=on includes Jewish year boundaries.

claims.claim: Hebcal holidays endpoint with the year derived from the shell date command.
claims.raw_snippet: The /hebcal endpoint year parameter can be set from $(date +%Y) in a bash step.

claims.claim: The Hebcal Shabbat endpoint for geonameid 281184 (Jerusalem) returns candle-lighting and havdalah times as JSON.
claims.raw_snippet: The /shabbat endpoint with cfg=json and geonameid returns Shabbat candle-lighting and havdalah times.

claims.claim: Hebcal Shabbat endpoint with M=on uses a fixed Havdalah of 50 minutes after sunset.
claims.raw_snippet: The /shabbat endpoint M=on parameter sets Havdalah to a fixed number of minutes after sunset.

claims.claim: Hebcal Shabbat endpoint with maj=on includes major holidays alongside Shabbat times.
claims.raw_snippet: The /shabbat endpoint maj=on parameter includes major Jewish holidays.

claims.claim: Templated Hebcal Shabbat endpoint with an {ID} geonameid placeholder.
claims.raw_snippet: The /shabbat endpoint geonameid is shown as an {ID} placeholder to be substituted per city.

claims.claim: Shell-variable Hebcal Shabbat endpoint used inside bash steps.
claims.raw_snippet: The /shabbat endpoint geonameid is set from the $GEONAMEID shell variable inside a workflow step.

claims.claim: Vercel supports pinning deployment regions (e.g. fra1 Frankfurt) documented in the Edge Network regions page.
claims.raw_snippet: Vercel regions include fra1 (Frankfurt). Functions and deployments can target specific regions.
